title: A formally unramified ring map has a universal first order thickening (algebra)
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings which is formally unramified: for every $R$-algebra $A$, every ideal $I\subseteq A$ with $I^2=0$ and every $R$-algebra map $a:S\to A/I$ there is at most one $R$-algebra map $a':S\to A$ with $q\circ a'=a$, where $q:A\to A/I$ is the quotient map. Then there exist an $R$-algebra $S'$ and a surjective $R$-algebra map $\pi:S'\to S$ whose kernel $K$ satisfies $K^2=0$, with the following universal property: for every $R$-algebra $A$, every ideal $I\subseteq A$ with $I^2=0$ (quotient map $q:A\to A/I$) and every $R$-algebra map $a:S\to A/I$, there is exactly one $R$-algebra map $a':S'\to A$ with $q\circ a'=a\circ\pi$. The pair $(S',\pi)$ is unique up to unique isomorphism of $R$-algebras compatible with the maps to $S$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 04EB (label lemma-universal-thickening, in Section 04EA 'Conormal modules and universal thickenings', section-conormal), with the uniqueness remark following it; formally unramified as in Algebra, Definition 00UN (definition-formally-unramified); the proof uses Lemma 00UO (lemma-characterize-formally-unramified: equivalent to Omega_{S/R}=0)
